dominant_strengths: Clear typographic hierarchy with the orange eyebrow date and bold 'Today' anchoring the view confidently
Restrained pastel tag palette (Design/Work/Engineering) reads as a coherent system without competing with task text
Completed-task treatment via strikethrough plus muted green check is legible and restful
dominant_weaknesses: Layout is a centered column floating in vast empty canvas — feels like a mockup frame, not a real product surface
Section headers ('Morning', 'Work') with emoji feel generic and indistinguishable from countless Things/Todoist clones
Status dots (red/orange/blue) are tiny and undersignified — meaning is unclear without a legend
fix_priorities: Commit to a real container width and chrome — sidebar, edges, or full-bleed — so it stops reading as a Figma artboard
Differentiate from the Things-lookalike pattern via a distinctive interaction or information layer (timeline, energy, focus)
Codify the colored status dot semantics with a subtle key or shape language so users can decode priority at a glance
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral clarity leads, visceral is pleasant-but-derivative, and reflective payoff is thin because nothing here makes the user feel their day differently.
rationale.intent_fit: It executes a competent task list but the brief asked for an 'original' take, and this lands squarely in familiar Things/Todoist territory.
